scenes.dialogue: You file a civil suit to protect your land. Before it is even registered, the judge decides you are likely to lose, and rejects it. Can a court do that?
The plaintiff says his sale deed was only security for a loan. The trial court found no buy-back clause and rejected his plaint, and the High Court agreed. So who was right?
Hi, I'm Ravishankar from LawWorld. On the fifth of November, Honourable Justice Ujjal Bhuyan and Honourable Justice Atul S Chandurkar ruled.
scenes.shown: Hi, I'm Ravishankar from LawWorld. On 5 November, Honourable Justice Ujjal Bhuyan and Honourable Justice Atul S. Chandurkar ruled.

scenes.dialogue: The plaintiff says his son settled the land on him. Needing money, he says, he borrowed twenty five lakh rupees from the defendant's husband, at twenty four percent a month.
scenes.shown: The plaintiff says his son settled the land on him. Needing money, he says, he borrowed ₹25 lakh from the defendant's husband, at 24% a month.
scenes.chip: 2 · A LOAN AND A SALE DEED

scenes.dialogue: He says the sale deed was only security for the loan, and he stayed in possession. When he offered to repay, he says, the land was not returned. So he sued.
Before the suit got a number, the District Judge at Cuddalore rejected the plaint. The sale deed had no resale clause, and no resale agreement was filed.
The Madras High Court agreed, for lack of cause of action. The defendant called it a real sale. The plaintiff argued no plaint can be rejected before registration.

scenes.dialogue: Finally, what did the Supreme Court decide? A plaint can be rejected even before registration, but not because the court thinks the suit will fail after trial.
This plaint disclosed a cause of action, so it was restored for registration, with no view on merits. And rejections before registration must be recorded.
